The Hacker News community generally responded to this project enabling apps on Kobo e-readers with positive reactions. stories.groq_explain: Kobo e-readers can now run third-party apps thanks to Cobalt, an open-source platform that turns the device into a mini computer. It’s like installing an app store on your e-reader—apps install, update, and remove wirelessly, and you can always go back to the normal Kobo reader. The apps are secure, running in isolated processes, and don’t mess with the device’s core functions. It matters because it turns a simple e-reader into a more versatile tool for reading, coding, or browsing without needing extra hardware.
